subject.title: Slack button interactions should dispatch a reply turn, not a heartbeat wake (follow-up to #99544)

question: Should Slack reply button/select clicks remain heartbeat-owned system events, or should Slack synthesize normal inbound reply turns for user-initiated controls?
rationale: Current source proves the path is still heartbeat-owned, but changing it replaces a recently accepted Slack system-event design and must preserve plugin interactive handlers, native approvals, thread routing, and related session-conflict handling.

options.title: Move Reply Controls To Inbound Turns
options.body: Treat user-initiated Slack reply controls like normal channel input and require regression proof for clicked value, thread delivery, and busy-run coalescing.

options.title: Keep Heartbeat And Harden It
options.body: Retain the system-event heartbeat design but require proof that values, visible replies, and retry behavior are reliable end to end.

options.title: Wait For Shared Conflict Repair
options.body: Defer the delivery-shape change until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102400 decides the shared reply-session conflict owner boundary.

recommendation.title: Move Reply Controls To Inbound Turns
recommendation.body: Treat user-initiated Slack reply controls like normal channel input and require regression proof for clicked value, thread delivery, and busy-run coalescing.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses the core system-event drain path and the predecessor closure that separated value surfacing from the remaining delivery-owner question.
